properties.description:
`flow:release-cut` — eight ordered steps with their TRIGGERS transitions, read back by `flow_report`. reflow2 dogfooding `cap:model-process` on itself: before 2026-08-21 this design contained ZERO Flow nodes, having shipped the vocabulary and never used it.

WHY IT HAD TO BE RECORDED RATHER THAN COMPUTED. `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` refused a START-HERE file because orientation is derivable. Release steps are NOT derivable from the graph: which registry, which workflow, which credential, what the tag format is, which files carry a version claim. Those are facts about the world outside the design, and no projection can compute them. The same derivability test that forbade the one argues for this.

WHAT IT REPLACES. The seven steps existed only in an agent's private session notes, recovered for the v0.19.0 cut from `git show v0.18.0` plus grepping AGENTS.md for "release". At least three were unguessable from the repo: the upgrade note is owed if and only if the schema stamp moved; the manifest must be complete rather than hand-typed; the Release needs an AT_EPOCH edge and creating the epoch node is not enough. Every one of those was learned by getting it wrong.

THE COST OF NOT HAVING IT, MEASURED: v0.17.0 shipped with no epoch edge and still lacks one; v0.19.0 repeated that four hours before `changelog_view` needed it; v0.20.0's export was stamped with the previous version; v0.22.0's changelog silently dropped 35 shipping changes; and v0.38.0 was published with an empty manifest. Five cuts, five different steps, each recorded only after it failed.

DISTINCT FROM the requirement it satisfies: that obliges ANY design holding Releases to record how it ships, and is a general rule reflow2 may one day detect the absence of in a user's project. This is reflow2's own instance of complying with it — one Flow, about this repo's cut, naming this repo's registries and files. The requirement would still stand if this Flow were deleted.
properties.name: reflow2's own release procedure is recorded as a Flow, so a cut is read from the design rather than from the last one
